functions.name: claim
functions.doc:
Release a paid invoice to its payee. Callable only by the payee, only
 while the link is `PAID`, and only once.

 Requires exactly 1 yoctoNEAR, which NEP-141 passes on to `ft_transfer`.

functions.name: create_link
functions.doc:
Record an invoice. Holds no funds and grants nobody a withdrawal; it
 only writes down what someone is owed.

type_schema.description:
NEAR Account Identifier.

This is a unique, syntactically valid, human-readable account identifier on the NEAR network.

[See the crate-level docs for information about validation.](index.html#account-id-rules)

Also see [Error kind precedence](AccountId#error-kind-precedence).

## Examples

``` use near_account_id::AccountId;

let alice: AccountId = "alice.near".parse().unwrap();

assert!("ƒelicia.near".parse::<AccountId>().is_err()); // (ƒ is not f) ```

functions.name: ft_on_transfer
functions.doc:
NEP-141 receiver hook. Returns the number of tokens *not* consumed:
 returning `amount` hands everything back to the sender (the token
 contract refunds automatically), returning `0` means it was all used.

 Every rejection path returns the full amount, so a failed payment costs
 the payer nothing.

functions.name: new
functions.doc:
Initialise the contract and register it as a balance holder with every
 allowlisted token.

 Registration is not optional. NEP-141's reference implementation panics
 when either side of a transfer is unregistered, so without it every
 incoming payment (`ft_transfer_call` to this contract) and every
 `claim` (`ft_transfer` from this contract) would fail. The attached
 deposit funds one NEP-145 storage balance per allowlisted token.

functions.name: on_claimed
functions.doc:
Settles `claim`. On failure the invoice returns to `PAID` so the payee
 can simply retry — the money is never lost and never double-sent.

Link.description: One invoice. Borsh-serialized at rest, JSON-serialized when read.

amount.description: Invoiced amount, in the token's base units.

creator.description: Who is owed the money. Also the only account allowed to `claim`.

paid_amount.description: What actually arrived — may exceed `amount` if the payer overpaid.

Status.description:
Lifecycle of an invoice.

`Expired` is never stored: it is derived on read from `expires_at`, so a link that quietly ages out is reported honestly without a background job having to rewrite it.
